chunks: Muhammad ibn Qays said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who gives preference to some of his children over others. He said: Yes, and also his wives.

key_terms.نِسَاءٌ: wives; in context of bequest, refers to a man's wives who may not otherwise receive from the estate
key_terms.وُلْدٌ: children (used broadly for male and female offspring)
key_terms.يُفَضِّلُ: to give preference or superiority to one over another in inheritance or bequest

ai.seo_question: Can a father give more inheritance to some children than others in Islam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Qays reports asking Imam al-Baqir (AS) whether a testator may legally favor certain children over others in a bequest. The Imam affirms this is permissible, and further adds that a man may likewise give preferential bequests to his wives. This hadith establishes the permissibility of unequal distribution in voluntary bequests (as distinguished from mandatory inheritance shares), providing a basis in Shia jurisprudence for testamentary freedom in allocating the permissible one-third of an estate.
